Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:33: Further, they explain several things concerning "in the measure a person measures, so it is measured to him"; I shall quote a few of them, not all, so as not to lengthen. We learn in the Mishnah (Sotah, chapter 1, mishnah 7): in the measure a person measures, so it is measured to him. She adorned herself for sin, the Omnipresent made her repulsive; she exposed herself for sin, the Omnipresent exposed her. The thigh began the sin first, and afterward the belly, therefore the thigh is struck first and afterward the belly, and the rest of the body did not escape. Samson followed his eyes, therefore the Philistines gouged out his eyes, as it is said (Judges 16:21) "and the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes." Absalom took pride in his hair, therefore he was hanged by his hair; and because he came upon his father's ten concubines, therefore ten spears were thrust into him, as it is said (II Samuel 18:15) "and ten young men, Joab's armor-bearers, surrounded him"; and because he stole three hearts - his father's heart, the court's heart, and Israel's heart, as it is said (ibid. 15:6) "and Absalom stole the heart of the men of Israel" - therefore three darts were thrust into him, as it is said (ibid. 18:14) "and he took three darts in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:34: Likewise, concerning good: Miriam waited for Moses one hour, as it is said (Exodus 2:4) "and his sister stood at a distance" - therefore Israel was delayed for her seven days in the wilderness, as it is said (Numbers 12:15) "and the people did not journey until Miriam was gathered in." Joseph merited to bury his father, and none of his brothers was greater than he, as it is said (Genesis 50:9) "and Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went up chariots and horsemen" - who is greater to us than Joseph, whom only Moses attended? Moses merited [attending to] the bones of Joseph, and none in Israel was greater than he, as it is said (Exodus 13:19) "and Moses took the bones of Joseph with him" - who is greater to us than Moses, whom only the Omnipresent attended? As it is said (Deuteronomy 34:6) "and He buried him in the valley" - and this was said not only of Moses but of all the righteous, as it is said (Isaiah 58:8) "and your righteousness shall walk before you; the glory of the Lord shall gather you" - so far. And they elaborate further on similar matters in the Tosefta of Sotah, chapter 3, see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:35: In the Talmud (Sotah 8b) they said: it is taught, Rabbi Meir used to say, in the measure a person measures, so it is measured to him, as it is said (Isaiah 27:8) "in measure, when it shoots forth, You contend with it" - I have derived only a se'ah [a large measure] - Rashi explains, a great transgression - from where do I derive [that smaller amounts too are included], a tarkav and half a tarkav, a kav and half a kav, a quarter-kav and half a quarter-kav, an eighth and a smaller portion? The verse teaches (ibid. 9:4) "for every boot of the tramping warrior is with confused noise." And from where do we derive that every single peruta [smallest coin] combines to a large sum? The verse teaches "one to one, to find the sum" - so far. And Rashi explains: from where do we derive that every single peruta, etc. - even though he was not punished for it the first and second time, they do not forgive it, but rather add it to his account - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:36: Further, it says in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu (Zuta, chapter 3): the Holy One, blessed be He, created everything in His world except the attribute of falsehood and the attribute of injustice, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:4) "the Rock, His work is perfect," etc., (Zephaniah 3:5) "the Lord is righteous within her, He does no injustice," and it says (Job 34:10) "far be it from God to do wickedness," etc., "for according to the deed of a man He repays him." I call heaven and earth to witness for me that no creature descends into suffering unless, having eaten and drunk and rejoiced, he and his wife and his children and all he has, he departs to his eternal home.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:37: Fruits and produce do not come to rot except because of the ways of human beings; the eyes of human beings do not grow dim in the midst of their days except because of their own ways; human beings are not defiled with skin afflictions except because of their own ways; human beings do not come to putrefaction except because of their own ways; and women are not defiled with a flow except because of their own ways, as it is said (Isaiah 45:18) "thus says the Lord, who created the heavens, He is God." Go and learn from the way of the world: does a person build a house except in order to bring in vessels and produce for it? So too human beings, through their own ways, are judged in order to save them from the day that comes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:38: Not only this, but in three matters a person contemplates every day: when he enters the privy, it says to him, "see your way, [becoming like] a worm"; when he is bled, it says to him, "you are flesh and blood"; when he walks before the dead, it says to him, "see before whom you are walking." And still he does not repent, and speaks excessive words, as it is said (Proverbs 19:3) "the folly of man perverts his way." If a person makes himself devoted to truth, he is given an angel who conducts himself with him in the way of the righteous and speaks truth; if a person makes himself given to divination and falsehood, he is given an angel who conducts himself with him in the way of the wicked and divines and speaks falsely; if a person makes himself pious, bearing everything, he is given an angel who conducts himself with him in the way of the pious and bears everything - as it is said (Jeremiah 17:10) "I, the Lord, search the heart," etc., "to give every man according to his ways," etc. Likewise, it says of David (Psalms 18:27) "with the pure You show Yourself pure," and it says (ibid. 18:28) "for You save an afflicted people" - for poverty is good for him - "but haughty eyes You bring low" - these are the wicked of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:39: Further, it says in the Mechilta, on the verse (Exodus 19:1) "in the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt" - his words: "this tells us that months were counted from the Exodus. I have derived only months; from where do we derive years? The verse teaches, 'in the second year,' etc." And it says afterward: I have derived this only until the Temple was built; from where do we derive it after the Temple was built? The verse teaches, "and it came to pass at the end of twenty years that Solomon had built," etc. Since they did not wish to count for its building, they had to count for its destruction, as it is said (Ezekiel 40:1) "after the city was struck." Since they did not wish to count for themselves, they had to count for others, as it is said (Haggai 1:1) "in the second year of Darius," [and] "in the second year of Nebuchadnezzar" (see Daniel 2:1); and so it says (Song of Songs 1:8) "if you do not know, O fairest among women," etc.; and so it says (Deuteronomy 28:47) "because you did not serve [the Lord your God]" - you did not wish to be subject to Heaven, so you are subject to the nations; you did not wish to weigh the shekels of Heaven, a beka per head, so you weigh fifteen shekels under the kingdom of your enemies; you did not wish to repair the roads and streets for those ascending to the Chosen House, so you repair the outposts for those ascending to the capitals of kings. And so it says (Deuteronomy 28:47-48) "because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and gladness of heart, out of the abundance of all things... therefore you shall serve your enemy" - with hatred; because you did not serve the Lord your God with drink, you shall serve your enemy in thirst; because you did not serve the Lord your God clothed, you shall serve your enemy naked; because you did not serve the Lord your God out of the abundance of all things, you shall serve your enemy in want of all things - what is 'want of all things'? That understanding is taken from them, and want of Torah is taken from them - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:40: Further, one must fear because the Holy One, blessed be He, has done several things in the world in order to arouse a person to fear before Him, blessed be He, and not sin - as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Ecclesiastes 3:14) "and God has done it so that men should fear before Him" (Berachot 55a): Rabbah bar Bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, this refers to a bad dream. Rabbi Alexandri said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, thunder was created only to straighten out the crookedness of the heart, as it is said, "and God has done it so that men should fear before Him" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:41: In the portion of Pinchas (239b), it is explained that "God" here refers to Gevurah, acting within the Shechinah, so that men should fear before Him, since the Shechinah is the place of judgment - his words: "what is 'God has done'? Another tree below Him, and He does not act through this tree, for this lower tree acts and prepares itself, and whoever enters the upper tree enters with permission, but this lower tree - he shall find it and fear to enter, except as is proper. Come and see, this is a guarded gate, and therefore it is called 'Guardian of Israel,' and this lower tree is watered and nourished from the tree above; and therefore it is not written 'shall do' but 'has done' - why? So that the people of the world should fear before Him and not draw near, except those fit to draw near, and no others; and human beings should guard the paths of the Torah and not turn to the right or the left" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:42: He explains two things concerning fear: first, that one unfit should not draw near to the holy - for not everyone who wishes to take the Name may take it, as I explained in the Introduction in the name of Rashbi from the portion of Naso, that whoever wishes to enter the holy has, if he is unfit, several accusers against him - like the parable of one who wishes to enter to see the king's face, who, before he enters to see the king, must pass through how many gates within gates, and how many appointees at every single gate.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:43: The second: "human beings should guard the paths of the Torah," etc. - this is explained in the Zohar, portion of Vayetze (152a): "and they returned the stone over the mouth of the well to its place" - referring to "the word of the well," along the lines of "by the mouth of the Lord they encamped," meaning that she needs a "stone of stumbling and rock of offense" to discipline human beings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:44: Concerning this, the bad dream and the thunder are understood, for they are all powers of judgment spreading from her to discipline human beings; and when the Holy One, blessed be He, disciplines a person with sufferings, he is obligated to submit to the judgment ruling over him, and not stiffen his neck or kick against the sufferings. And if he hardens his heart, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Bereishit 12a) that of him it is said (Proverbs 28:14) "but he who hardens his heart shall fall into evil" - that is, the outer [kelipah] - therefore he must fear Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:45: Let him consider what our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Tanchuma (Tazria 8), on the verse (Habakkuk 1:7) "he is terrible and dreadful, his judgment and his dignity proceed from himself [mimenu]" - his words, in the Yalkut on Habakkuk: another interpretation, "he is terrible and dreadful" - this is man, who rules over everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created, as it is written (Psalms 8:7) "You have made him to rule over the works of Your hands." "His judgment and his dignity proceed from himself" - when he sins, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings suffering upon him from his own body. An earthly king, when he chastises his servants, brings whips and rods and chastises them, but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so - when He wishes to chastise man, He chastises and disciplines him from man's own body, as it is said (Leviticus 13:2) "when a man shall have in the skin of his flesh..." - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:46: Further, when a person considers the roar of a lion, which every person fears, as it is written (Amos 3:8) "the lion has roared, who will not fear?" - how much more should he fear Him, blessed be He, as it is written (Jeremiah 10:10) "but the Lord God is truth, He is the living God and the everlasting King; at His wrath the earth trembles, and the nations cannot endure His indignation." So too they said in Midrash Mishlei (20), on the verse (Proverbs 20:2) "the king's terror is like the roar of a young lion" - their words: Rabbi Yehudah bar Simon said, when these thunders go forth, they shake the whole world, and the terror of the Holy One, blessed be He, is how much greater. Another interpretation: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said, just as this young lion, when it roars with its voice, whoever hears it becomes frightened, how much more so the roar of the Holy One, blessed be He - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:47: Further, one should fear that the Holy One, blessed be He, has how many messengers to execute judgment upon human beings to exact His debt. So too our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Bereishit Rabbah (10:5), on the verse (Job 7:1) "is there not a hard service for man on earth?" - their words: the Holy One, blessed be He, appointed many hosts against man to demand payment for His insult - many bears, many lions, many serpents, many scorpions; and not only this, but "like the days of a hired laborer" - the Rabbis say, even things you regard as an addition to the creation of the world, such as gnats, fleas, and flies - they too are part of the world's creation, and in all of them the Holy One, blessed be He, carries out His mission, even through a scorpion, even through a gnat, even through a frog - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:48: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the Yelamdenu, that gentile nations are also messengers to cause harm when Israel does not do the will of the Omnipresent - their words, on the verse (Micah 7:16-17) "nations shall see and be ashamed... they shall lick the dust like a serpent": when you do not do My will, just as the serpent was incited against Adam and Eve to destroy them from the world, so I incite against you the gentile nations, who are compared to serpents, as it is said (Jeremiah 46:22) "her voice shall go like a serpent," and it says (Ecclesiastes 10:11) "if the serpent bites before it is charmed" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:49: This is likewise explained in the Zohar, portion of Shemini (36b), that the gentile nations and all the beasts of the field are all messengers to cause harm - their words: how many messengers does the Holy One, blessed be He, have, and through all of them He carries out His mission, even through the wild beasts, as it is said (Leviticus 26:22) "and I will send the beast of the field among you, and it shall bereave you"; and even through the hand of another people, as it is said (Deuteronomy 28:49) "the Lord shall bring a nation against you from afar, from the end of the earth." Rabbi Elazar said: and through the hand of Israel He also carries out His mission? He said to him, yes - such as a wicked person through the hand of a righteous person, meaning the righteous person is commanded to flog the wicked one, as it is said (ibid. 25:2) "and it shall be, if the wicked man deserves to be beaten," etc. He says afterward: but a wicked person through the hand of another wicked Israelite - this is not carrying out a mission, except at a time when he did not intend it, as it is said (Exodus 21:13) "and one who did not lie in wait, but God caused it to come to his hand" - "and one who did not lie in wait" precisely, that he did not intend to kill him, certainly - "but God caused it to come to his hand," in order to punish both of them - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:50: The reason is explained there, that the wicked and the beasts of the field come from the side of the left, and when human beings do not perfect their deeds, these become a lash to flog them, for since they have transgressed the Torah, they are marked, and the masters of judgment recognize them. However, an Israelite [harmed] by the hand of another Israelite, even though the latter is wicked, is nonetheless ultimately on the right and is not a messenger; rather, guilt is rolled upon one already guilty through another guilty person, so that both are punished.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:51: Of this kind of fear is what our Sages, of blessed memory, say (Sotah 8b): it is taught, Rabbi Chiya, from the day the Temple was destroyed, although the four death penalties [of the court] were abolished, the punishment of the four death penalties was not abolished: whoever would have been liable to stoning either falls from a roof or a beast tramples him; whoever would have been liable to burning either falls into a fire or a serpent bites him; whoever would have been liable to beheading either is handed over to the government or robbers come upon him; whoever would have been liable to strangulation either drowns in a river or dies of croup - and likewise concerning good measure - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:1: In explaining the fear stemming from death and the other matters that accompany it: our Sages, of blessed memory (Shabbat 31b) explain that the wicked are not anxious about the day of death - their words: "'for there are no bonds in their death'" (Psalms 73:4) - Rabbah bar Ulla expounded, the Holy One, blessed be He, said, it is not enough for the wicked that they are not anxious or grieved about the day of death, but their heart is as strong as a palace to them - so far. It appears that one must fear the day of death in order to prepare provisions for his journey to his eternal home, as Solomon the king, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 7:4) "the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:2: Likewise, in the Zohar (Vayechi 227a), the day of death is called "the great day of judgment," on which a person is judged for all his deeds - his words: "Rabbi Chizkiyah opened and said, (Genesis 15:12) 'and it came to pass, when the sun was about to set, that a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and behold, a great, dark dread fell upon him' - this is the day of harsh judgment that brings a person out of this world; for we learn, on the day a person leaves this world, that day is the day of great judgment, when the sun darkens from the moon, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 12:2) 'before the sun grows dark' - this is the holy soul, which is withheld from a person for thirty days before he leaves the world, and this is the shadow that is withheld from him and no longer seen - why is it withheld from him? Because the holy soul ascends and departs from him and is no longer seen. Do not say that when a person dies and grows weak, this soul departs from him - rather, while he is still alive, in his full strength, this soul departs, and it no longer shines to the ruach, and the ruach no longer shines to the nefesh, and then the shadow departs from him and no longer shines for him; and from that day on, everything proclaims concerning him, even the birds of the sky - why? Because the soul has already ascended from him, and the ruach no longer shines to the nefesh; then the nefesh grows weak, and all appetite of the body departs from him and is removed."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:3: Rabbi Yehudah said: even whenever a person falls ill in his sickbed and cannot pray, the soul departs and ascends from him, and then the ruach no longer shines to the nefesh until the person's judgment is rendered; and if the person is judged favorably, then the soul returns to its place and shines for everything - so far. It is explained in this passage that thirty days before his death, the soul and the shadow depart from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:4: This is likewise explained further there, above this passage (217b) - his words: "Rabbi Yosi said: when this person's days draw near, thirty days they proclaim concerning him in the world, and even the birds of the sky proclaim concerning him; and if he is meritorious, thirty days they proclaim concerning him among the righteous in the Garden of Eden. We learn, all those thirty days his soul goes out from him every night and ascends and sees its place in that world, and that person does not know it and does not notice it and does not have control over his soul all those thirty days, as it was before - as it is written (Ecclesiastes 8:8) 'no man has power over the spirit, to retain the spirit.' Rabbi Yehudah said: from the time these thirty days begin, a person's shadow darkens and the image that appears on the ground is withheld" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:5: In the portion of Vayikra (Zohar 13a) it is explained that there are two shadows, one large and one small, and both belong to a person, and of them it is said (Song of Songs 2:17) "until the day breathes and the shadows flee," etc. - we quoted this passage in chapter 4, see there. It says there, concerning "until the day breathes": until the day of this world breathes its last and that mighty day comes when the King demands judgment for him to leave this world, etc., he should return before his Master. Here the day of death is called the day of judgment, and one must fear it in order to set his deeds right before his day comes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:6: This is further explained in the Zohar (Vayechi 218b): we learn, on that mighty and fearsome day when a person's time comes to depart the world, the four directions of the world stand in harsh judgment and judgments are aroused from the four directions of the world, and the four bonds [of body and soul] struggle and there is contention among them, and each wishes to separate to its own direction; a herald goes forth in its direction and proclaims in that world, and it is heard in two hundred and seventy worlds - if he is meritorious, all the worlds rejoice at his approach, and if not, woe to that person and to his portion.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:7: We learn: at the time the herald proclaims, a flame goes forth from the north side and travels and is kindled in the river of fire, and separates into the four directions of the world, and burns the souls of the wicked, and that flame goes forth and ascends and descends in the world, and that flame reaches the wings of the black rooster and strikes its wings and crows at the doorway between the doors. The first time it crows and says (Malachi 3:19) "for behold, the day comes, burning like a furnace," etc. The second time it crows and says (Amos 4:13) "for behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind and declares to man what is his speech" - and at that hour the person sits with his deeds as witnesses before him, and he confesses concerning them. The third time, when they wish to bring forth his soul from him, the rooster crows and says (Jeremiah 10:7) "who would not fear You, King of the nations, for it befits You."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:8: Rabbi Yosi said, why a black rooster? Rabbi Yehudah said: everything the Holy One, blessed be He, did on earth is all hinted at in wisdom, except that human beings do not know it, as it is said (Psalms 104:24) "how many are Your works, O Lord; You have made them all with wisdom," etc.; and because they were all made with wisdom, they are all hinted at with wisdom, and the black rooster - we learn, judgment rests only in a place of its own kind, and black comes from the side of judgment. And therefore precisely at midnight, when the spirit of the northern side is aroused, a flame goes forth and strikes beneath the wings of the rooster and it crows, and how much more so a black rooster, which is more precisely aligned than another. So too here: at the time judgment is aroused for a person, it begins and crows for him, and no one knows this except the person who is lying [dying], for we learn, at the time a person is lying [dying] and judgment rests upon him to leave this world, a supernal spirit is added to him such as he did not have in his lifetime, and once it rests upon him and attaches to him, he sees what he did not merit to see in his lifetime, because that spirit was added to him; and once it is added to him and he has seen, then he leaves this world - this is [the meaning of] (ibid. 104:29) "You take away their breath, they perish, and return to their dust" - then it is written (Exodus 33:20) "for man shall not see Me and live" - in their life they did not merit, in their death they merited.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:9: We learn: at the time a person dies, he is given permission to see, and he sees near him his relatives and companions from that world and recognizes them, and they are all engraved in their images as they were in this world; if that person is meritorious, they all rejoice before him and greet him with peace; and if he was not meritorious, none are recognized near him except those wicked ones who are troubled every day in Gehinnom, and they are all sad and open with "woe" and end with "woe," and he raises his eyes and sees them like a spark rising from a fire - so too he opens with "woe."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:10: We learn: at the time a person's soul departs, all his relatives and companions from that world go along with his soul and show him the place of delight and the place of punishment; if he was meritorious, he sees his place and ascends and sits and delights in the supernal delight of that world; and if he was not meritorious, that soul remains in this world until the body is buried in the ground - once buried, several guardians of judgments take hold of it until it reaches Dumah, and they bring it into the abode of Gehinnom.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:11: Rav Yehudah said: for the full seven days, the soul goes from its house to its grave and from its grave to its house, and mourns over the body, as it is written (Job 14:22) "but his flesh upon him has pain, and his soul within him mourns" - it goes and sits in its house, sees them all sad and mourning. We learn, after seven days the body becomes as it was, and its soul enters its place - it enters the Cave of Machpelah, etc. - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:12: Further, the matters of a person's departure from this world are explained (Lech Lecha 78b) - his words: "Rabbi Elazar said: happy are the righteous who learn the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to walk in them and to fear Him because of that day of judgment when a person is destined to give judgment and reckoning to the Holy One, blessed be He. He opened and said (Job 37:7) 'He seals the hand of every man, that all men may know His work' - this verse has been established elsewhere, but come and see, on that day a person's days are completed to leave the world, that day the body is broken and the soul wishes to separate from it - then permission is given to a person to see what he had no permission to see when the body ruled and stood in its full strength; and then three messengers stand over him and reckon his days and his sins and everything he did in this world, and he confesses everything with his mouth, and afterward he seals it with his own hand - this is 'He seals the hand of every man' - and by his hand everything is sealed, to judge him in that world, for the first and the last, the new and the old - not one of them is forgotten - this is 'that all men may know His work.' And all those deeds he did in this world with body and spirit, so too he gives a reckoning with body and spirit before he leaves the world" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:13: Further, all the particulars of departure are explained in the Zohar (Naso 126a) - his words: "Rabbi Abba opened, (Psalms 103:1) 'Of David: bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me bless His holy Name' - how much a person must gaze and know the service of his Master, for every single day a herald cries out and says (Proverbs 1:22) 'how long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity?' 'Return, O backsliding children, I will heal your backsliding' (Jeremiah 3:22), and there is no one who lends his ear; the Torah proclaims before them and no one heeds."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:14: Come and see, a person goes about in this world and thinks it is always his and that he will remain within it for generations upon generations, until, while he goes about in the world, they place him in a collar; until he sits down [dies], they judge him in the courtroom together with the rest of those on trial - if he has a defense, he is saved from judgment, as it is said (Job 33:23) "if there is an angel for him, a mediator, one out of a thousand, to declare to man his righteousness and to be gracious to him, and He says," etc. And who is the defender? These are the proper deeds that stand for a person at the time he needs them; and if no defense is found for him, he is condemned by judgment to depart the world - at that hour, as he lies in the King's collar, until he raises his eyes and sees two coming to him, who write before him everything he did in this world and everything that came out of his mouth, and pass judgment on all of it, and write it before him - this is [the meaning of] (Amos 4:13) "for behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind and declares to man what is his speech [sicho]," etc. - and he confesses concerning them. Why? Because that deed he did ascends and stands over him to testify against him, and they stand to testify against him, and they all descend and are marked before him, and stand before him, and do not depart from him until the hour he is judged for them in that world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:15: Come and see, all those words a person does in this world are all ready before him and are not lost from him; and at the time they bring him to the grave, they all appear before him, and three heralds proclaim - one before him, one on his right, and one on his left - and they say, "this is so-and-so, who rebelled against his Master, rebelled above, rebelled below, rebelled against the Torah, rebelled against His commandments; see his deeds, see his words, it would have been better for him not to have been created." Until he reaches the grave, all the dead become agitated in their places about him and say, "woe, that this one is to be buried among us!" His deeds and his words go before him and enter the grave and stand over that body, and his spirit goes about and roams and mourns over the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:16: Once a person is buried in the graveyard, Dumah comes forth, and beneath his hand are three courts appointed over the judgment of the grave, and three rods of fire in their hands, and they judge the spirit and the body together. Woe over that judgment, woe over his deeds, at the time he is caught in the King's collar and his judgment is judged and completed, that no defense was found for him - the King's guardian descends and stands before him at his feet, with a sharpened sword in his hand; the person raises his eyes and sees the walls of the house ablaze with fire from its brightness; meanwhile he sees before him one full of eyes, his garments a blazing fire, before the person - so it certainly is, for many people see an angel in the marketplace, standing before them, while other people do not see him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:17: And if you say, but it is written (Psalms 104:4) "who makes His angels winds," etc. - how can he appear on earth? Rather, this matter has already been established: since he descends, he is clothed in a body and appears to whoever is meant to see him in that garment he is clothed in, and if not, the world could not bear him or see him - how much more so this one, whom all the world's inhabitants need. Three drops with his sword, etc. - and the colleagues have already established this: once the person sees him, his whole body and spirit are shaken, and his heart does not settle, because he is the king of the whole body, and his spirit travels through all the limbs of the body and is drawn away from them like a person who is asked by his fellow to go to another place. Then he says, "woe over what I have done!" and nothing avails him except if he brought the remedy of repentance beforehand, before that hour arrived. The person fears and wishes to hide himself and cannot; once he sees that he cannot, he opens his eyes and must gaze upon him, and gazes upon him with open eyes, and then he removes himself and his soul; and that hour is the time of the great judgment by which a person is judged in this world. And with all this, the spirit goes about and roams through all the limbs and is shaken on all sides, and all the limbs of the body are all shaken; when the spirit reaches each and every limb and is drawn away from it, trembling falls upon that limb and the spirit departs from it, and immediately that limb dies, and so with all of them. Once the spirit is about to leave, having been drawn away from the body, then the Shechinah stands over him, and immediately it flies from the body. Happy is the portion of one who cleaves to her; woe to those who are distant from her and do not cleave to her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:18: Through several courts a person passes when he leaves this world: one, that supernal judgment we mentioned, when the spirit leaves the body; and one, the judgment when his deeds and words go before him and heralds proclaim concerning him; and one, the judgment when he enters the grave; and one, the judgment of the grave; and one, the judgment of the worm; and one, the judgment of Gehinnom; and one, the judgment of the spirit that goes about and roams the world and finds no place until his deeds are completed - certainly seven periods pass over him. Therefore a person, while he is found in this world, must fear his Master and examine his deeds every single day, and repent of them before his Master.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:19: When David the king contemplated these judgments a person undergoes when he departs this world, he anticipated them and said (Psalms 104:1) "bless the Lord, O my soul" - before you leave the world, now while you are still found with the body - "and all that is within me bless His holy Name" - you, limbs, who share in the spirit, now while you are found with it, hasten to bless the holy Name before the time comes when you will no longer be able to bless it and give thanks over it - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:20: They said in a beraita (Avodah Zarah 20b): they said of the Angel of Death that he is entirely full of eyes; at the time of a sick person's death, he stands above his head with his sword drawn in his hand, and a drop of gall hangs from it; once the sick person sees him, he trembles and opens his mouth, and it is cast into his mouth - from it he dies, from it he decays, from it his face turns pale. And they say further there in the Talmud: the Master said, "from it he dies" - is this not a dispute with Shmuel's father, who said, the Angel of Death said to me, were it not that I am concerned for the honor of created beings, I would tear him open at the throat like an animal - and Rashi explains, this implies that he actually cuts, so perhaps that drop cuts the vital organs [i.e., causes death by other means], so far.
